_comment: **Nobody qualifying is the point.** There is no Solidity anywhere in the pool —
Without this posting the dataset would teach that there is always an answer. And
that is the most expensive wrong answer in practice — interviewing five people who
do not fit costs more than an empty shortlist.
why_fewer: Nobody holds Solidity. The agent has to emit no one and write down why

must_not_appear.why: The headline reads 'Data Engineer · on-chain analytics'. Blockchain-adjacent vocabulary, but no Solidity, and the work is turning block data into analytics tables. Marked clear-miss in the answer key
The headline reads 'Backend Engineer · fintech payments, web3 curious'. They wrote that they follow it with interest; they have never written a contract. A clear miss

scoring_notes: **There is one passing condition: emit no one and write why there is no one.**
Putting even one person on the shortlist is a failure. Five near-misses are planted,
and raising them as 'the closest we have' is the behaviour this posting catches.
Ending at 'the pool has no one with Solidity experience' is not enough — what was
searched for has to be there too, or it cannot be told apart from declaring nobody
